
 # Export plan

 The old CMS stores posts as HTML fragments in a single table, with images referenced by absolute
 URLs. The export has to keep every published URL working, because search engines and a few old
 forum threads still link to them. Drafts are not exported. They stay in the database dump in case
 one is worth finishing.

 ## Steps

 1. Dump the database from the read replica, never the primary.
 2. Convert each fragment to markdown with the script below.
 3. Download every image the posts reference into static/images/<year>/<slug>/.
 4. Rewrite the image links to the new relative paths.
 5. Diff a sample of twenty rendered posts against the live site.

 ## Conversion script

   mysqldump --single-transaction blog posts > posts.sql
   python3 convert.py --input posts.sql --output content/posts
   rg --count '<img' content/posts | sort -t: -k2 -n | tail -20

 The converter is idempotent, so a rerun after fixing one post rewrites only that post. Run it from
 the repository root, or the relative output path lands somewhere surprising.

 ## Where each field goes

  Field                         │ Old CMS                           │ Static site
 ───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────
  [esc]back [j/k]scroll [^d/^u]half page [g/G]top/bottom [space]done [e]dit [n]otes …        43/78
